description: Two-panel mechanical-property figure for a Fe-Mn-Al-C austenitic low-density steel hot-rolled to 45%, 68% and 82% reduction. (a) Engineering stress σ_e (y-axis, MPa, 0–1000 with ticks every 200) versus engineering strain ε_e (x-axis, 0.00–0.70, ticks every 0.10) with three smooth curves; the lower-right legend identifies them as HR45 (grey), HR68 (red) and HR82 (blue). All curves rise steeply, then plateau and soften. The blue HR82 curve is highest, peaking between the 900 and 1000 MPa gridlines at about ε = 0.39 and fracturing just before the 0.50 tick; the red HR68 curve peaks between the 900 and 1000 MPa gridlines near ε = 0.45 and ends near ε = 0.57; the grey HR45 curve is lowest, peaking between the 800 and 900 MPa gridlines near ε = 0.50 and extending to about ε = 0.63. Higher rolling reduction therefore raises flow stress while shortening elongation. (b) Charpy V-notch (CVN) impact energy (y-axis, printed as "J/m2", 100–140) versus hot-rolling reduction (%, 40–85, ticks every 5) showing three error-barred points on a monotonically descending line: ≈133 at 45%, ≈116 at 68% and ≈105 at 82% J/m2. The two panels together show strength increasing while ductility and toughness decrease only modestly with increasing reduction.

observations.observation: Panel (a) legend (lower right) labels the three stress-strain curves exactly as HR45 (grey), HR68 (red) and HR82 (blue).
In (a) the HR82 (blue) curve attains the highest engineering stress, peaking between the 900 and 1000 MPa gridlines, and fractures at the lowest strain, just before the 0.50 strain tick.
In (a) the HR45 (grey) curve is the lowest, peaking between the 800 and 900 MPa gridlines, and extends to the largest strain, about 0.63.
In (a) the HR68 (red) curve lies between the other two, peaking between the 900 and 1000 MPa gridlines and ending near ε = 0.57; its yield region starts near 620 MPa while HR82 starts near 700 MPa.
Panel (a) axes are labelled 'Engineering strain, ε_e' (0.00–0.70) and 'Engineering stress, σ_e (MPa)' (0–1000), and no numeric values are printed on the curves themselves.
In (b) the three error-barred CVN data points lie on a monotonic descending line, so impact energy decreases continuously as hot-rolling reduction increases from 45% to 82%.
The (b) y-axis unit is printed as 'J/m2' (Charpy V-notch impact energy) over the range 100–140, and the x-axis is 'Hot-rolling reduction (%)' over 40–85.
The caption describes (a) as engineering stress (σ)-strain (ε_e) curves and (b) as 'Chary [Charpy] V-notch (CVN)' impact energy as a function of hot-rolling reduction.
The citing text states the HR45 sample had a UTS of 861 ± 11 MPa, a YS of 480 ± 0 MPa and a total elongation of 60%.
The citing text states that increasing rolling reduction from 45% to 82% raised UTS by ~110 MPa and YS by ~170 MPa, while UE fell from 52.0 ± 1.0% to 39.0 ± 0.8% and TE from 60 ± 1% to 50 ± 1%.
The citing text states all three samples had a reduction of area >60%, indicating good ductility was retained.
The citing text states the CVN impact energy decreased from 133 ± 2.5 J/m² at 45% reduction to 105 ± 1.2 J/m² at 82% reduction, with all samples remaining above 100 J/m².
The citing text states that the two panels jointly support the conclusion that strength is enhanced while ductility and toughness decrease only slightly with increasing hot-rolling reduction.

subfigures.description: Engineering stress σ_e (MPa, 0–1000) versus engineering strain ε_e (0.00–0.70) with three curves, labelled in the lower-right legend as HR45 (grey), HR68 (red) and HR82 (blue). HR82 reaches the highest stress (between the 900 and 1000 MPa gridlines) and fails at the lowest strain (<0.50); HR45 is the lowest curve and the most ductile, extending to ~0.63 strain. No numeric data labels are printed.

Charpy V-notch (CVN) impact energy (y-axis labelled J/m2, 100–140) versus hot-rolling reduction (%, 40–85) with three error-barred points at ≈45%/133, ≈68%/116 and ≈82%/105 J/m2 joined by a descending straight trend line, showing a monotonic loss of impact energy as rolling reduction increases.

unreadable_items: Panel (a): no numeric data labels are printed on the curves; stress/strain values can only be read against the gridlines
Panel (b): the value of the middle (68% reduction) point is not labelled and must be read against the gridlines (lies between 115 and 120 J/m2)
